method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, reverse paraphrase of both contradiction branches, and exact formula, token, macro and cross-reference checks. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The two-argument halting function, self-input diagonal function, machine-composition contradiction, theorem and four exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A fixed machine enumeration gives each description an index. Cardinality ensures some noncomputable functions, but the halting function h is a specific 0/1 candidate: 0 when M_e does not halt on n and 1 when it does. The self-input function s has the same values at n=e. Its noncomputability will imply h's.
samples.checks: Both displayed case orders, the n-stroke input in the problem definition, and references to disciplined machines and composition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Assume a machine S computes s and choose a fully disciplined equivalent, hence one that halts on square one. Compose it with J, which halts on blank/zero and otherwise runs right forever. Let the composite be M_e. If M_e(e) halts, s(e)=1 makes S output one stroke and J diverge; if M_e(e) does not halt, s(e)=0 makes S output blank and J halt. Each case contradicts itself.
samples.checks: The e-self-input, direction of both case implications, blank representation of zero and composition S concat J are intact. Reader note OLTUR-008 corrects only the source's equivalence of one condition with the full four-clause disciplined definition.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If a hypothetical H computes h, copy input e with a blank separator and feed (e,e) to H. This would compute s, contrary to the preceding lemma; hence h is not Turing-computable and the Halting Problem has no solver.
samples.checks: The copier reference and the reduction direction h to s remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercises ask about the fixed three-stroke input problem, reducing diagonal cases to off-diagonal ones, using machine descriptions instead of indices, and the partial self-input function that returns 1 only on halting inputs and is undefined otherwise.
samples.checks: The last exercise says the partial function is computable, in contrast to the total 0/1 s; both equality/inequality cases and the three-stroke count are preserved.
